title: Repair Recorder & Playlet Factory for Interactive Admin Workflows
text:
Repair Recorder & Playlet Factory for Interactive Admin Workflows

description:
Implement a lightweight 'Repair Recorder' that captures operator actions (CLI commands, Console UI sequences, API calls) into parameterized, idempotent playlets that can be reviewed, dry-run, and re-executed by oncall or runbook automation. The Playlet Factory converts recorded traces into sanitized task definitions (runbooks-as-tasks) with safety gates, telemetry links, and RBAC checks so that common incident remediations can be surfaced in the Console as one-click or guided flows.

acceptance_criteria:
Recorder can capture a sequence of admin actions (CLI/API/Console) with timestamps and call parameters
Playlet Factory generates a parameterized runlet JSON that includes idempotency markers and pre/post checks
Generated playlets support dry-run mode that simulates actions without mutating production state
Playlets are surfaced in Console under 'Suggested Repairlets' with human-review workflow
Telemetry traces link playlet runs back to incident timelines and surface per-step success/failure metrics
RBAC enforcement prevents playlets from exposing or executing actions beyond assignee privileges
End-to-end test harness reproduces 90% of recorded sequences in staging with deterministic outcomes

implementation_notes:
Key components: capture agent (CLI proxy + UI event hook), sanitizer (secret stripping and normalizers), playlet generator (schema translation + idempotency heuristics), dry-run executor, console integration (review UI + provenance), telemetry correlation layer. Use existing admin-proxy infra (ENG-614972) as capture transport to minimize infra work.

risk_mitigation:
Do not auto-run any autogenerated playlet in production without a human review and two-step confirmation.
Default retention for raw recordings set to 7 days; require workspace-level opt-in for extended retention and audit logging.
Throttle playlet execution across Dedicated pools and require quota checks; fail closed if capacity signals are absent.
Instrument per-step rollback hooks; if any step fails, run compensating actions recorded in the playlet or revert to safe-state snapshot.

qa_notes:
Build replay harness in CI that runs generated playlets against a sandbox cluster. Include snapshot assertions for resource counts and API responses. Fallback: if playlet run mutates state unexpectedly, mark as non-reproducible and require manual triage. Create regression suite from the 50-sample corpus.

acceptance_test_steps:
Record an incident remediation session in staging that includes: 2 CLI actions, 1 API call, 1 Console click sequence
Run Playlet Factory to generate a playlet; verify schema validity and presence of idempotency_token
Execute playlet in dry-run and verify zero side-effects; confirm telemetry emits simulated-step events
Have reviewer approve and execute playlet in staging; assert final system state matches expected snapshot
Run a roll-forward and a roll-back scenario to validate compensating actions

updates:
2026-01-12 - Aisha: Initial spike completed. Proved viability of capturing CLI sessions via our existing admin proxy shim; prototype saved 1kB JSON per session with metadata.
2026-01-25 - Miles: Design review with Security. Decided to strip secrets at capture time and store only parameter names + hash. Security requested explicit KMS-backed envelope for any captured credential references.
2026-02-03 - Miles: Architecture doc posted to Confluence (link below). Chosen canonical 'playlet' schema that includes steps[], checks[], idempotency_token, telemetry_context.
2026-02-18 - Eng: Implemented dry-run engine and a mock executor for staging. Discovered three classes of non-determinism (time-based tokens, leader-election calls, external webhooks). Added normalizers for two types.
2026-02-28 - QA: Created replay harness and sample corpus of 50 recorded incidents. 38/50 reproducible without manual edits; plan: create heuristics to normalize remaining 12.
2026-03-05 - PM: Reviewed UX flows with Design. Agreed on 'suggested playlet' cards and a mandatory review step before first-run in a given workspace.


review_feedback:
PM (Jordan Lee): Keep the first experience discovery-focused — don't overwhelm oncall with too many autogenerated playlets; add confidence score and provenance metadata.
Security (Lena Correa): Strip secrets early; require explicit opt-in per workspace to persist replay artifacts longer than 7 days; KMS envelope must be used for any sensitive payload.
Design (Priya Menon): Show step-level telemetry and expected side-effects in the review UI; provide 'explain' affordance that maps each step to the incident symptoms it addresses.
SRE (Omar Hassan): Add a hard limit on parallel replay jobs in prod to avoid regeneration storms; recommend queueing and backoff policies tied to Dedicated capacity signals.

open_questions:
How should we compute and display the confidence score for an autogenerated playlet? (heuristics vs ML model)
What is the correct retention policy for recordings where a customer has regulatory requirements? (workspace opt-in with audit trails?)
Should certain high-risk admin actions (schema migrations, data deletions) be excluded from automatic playlet generation and instead surface as curated templates?
